idea: Issuer-sponsored research for UK small caps
buyer: IR directors and CFOs at AIM/small-cap listed companies
pain: No sell-side coverage since unbundling, so no investor visibility
v1: One sponsored initiation note for a single issuer
channel: Direct to IR teams and small-cap brokers
verdict: Strong ceiling and recurring, but the buyer is a corporate she does not know and cycles are slow.
ceiling_arithmetic: £30k/yr x 8 issuers = £240k. Eight retained issuers is a real business but each is a corporate sale into a company she has no relationship with.
carries: Genuinely proven model with an existing paying market, recurring annual retainers, and a ceiling that clears the bar.
kills: Distribution. Her network is the buy side; the buyer here is corporate IR, which is a cold segment for her.
test: Ask two small-cap brokers whether they would refer issuers, and two IR directors what they pay now.
test_pass: A broker offers to introduce issuers on a referral basis.
test_fail: Issuers already use Edison or Progressive and see no gap.

why.distribution: Her network is the buy side; the buyer here is corporate IR, a segment she must reach cold.
why.demand: Issuers already pay Edison and Progressive for exactly this - a worse substitute being paid for today.
why.fmf: Writing initiating coverage to institutional standard is precisely her eight-year trade.
why.revenue_structure: Annual retainers per issuer, renewing as long as the company stays listed.
why.defensibility: Established sponsored-research houses have the broker relationships; her edge is quality alone.
why.leverage: Each note is bespoke to an issuer, though her process compounds across them.
why.time_to_revenue: Corporate sales cycles plus broker introductions: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: The coverage gap that created this market is real, though FCA re-bundling may partly close it.
why.ceiling: £30k/yr x 8 issuers = £240k on recurring annual retainers - one of the few genuinely clearing shapes.
